merger_description:
RCT Solutions GmbH (**RCT Solutions**), based in Konstanz, Germany, is an independent German engineering house dedicated to consulting and engineering services for clients in the photovoltaic and battery manufacturing space. It offers end-to-end consulting, engineering, and ramp-up services for photovoltaic cells and modules as well as battery manufacturing plants. RCT Solutions has no Australian operations.

RCT Solutions is part of the wider RCT group, which is a privately held family of technology and manufacturing companies headquartered in Konstanz, Germany.

The vendor, Wärtsilä Finland Oy (the **Seller**), is a subsidiary of Finnish technology group Wärtsilä and is headquartered in Vaasa, Finland. It is a global manufacturer of combustion engines, propulsion systems, and power plants for the marine and energy sectors. The Seller currently holds 100% of the share capital in Wärtsilä Energy Storage Finland Oy (**Wärtsilä Energy**).

Wärtsilä Energy is headquartered in Helsinki, Finland. It is the energy storage business of the Finnish technology group Wärtsilä and acts as a system integrator, combining battery cells from leading manufacturers with its own energy management software, power conversion technology, controls, and lifecycle services to deliver complete, utility-scale battery energy storage solutions for modern power systems.

Wärtsilä Energy supplies equipment into Australia directly, and provides services to customers domestically through its wholly owned local subsidiary, Wärtsilä Energy Storage Australia Pty Ltd.

Pursuant to a Share Purchase Agreement, RCT Solutions will acquire from the Seller 50% of the shares in Wärtsilä Energy (the **Acquisition**). The Acquisition will establish a joint venture with the Seller retaining the remaining 50%. Post-acquisition, the Seller and RCT Solutions will jointly control Wärtsilä Energy.

determination_table_content.details:
RCT Solutions GmbH (RCT Solutions) applied for a notification
waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of 50% of the share
capital in Wärtsilä Energy Storage Finland Oy (Wärtsilä Energy), as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, RCT Solutions, is an independent engineering house
based in Konstanz, Germany, dedicated to consulting and
engineering services for clients in the photovoltaic and battery
manufacturing space. It offers end-to-end consulting, engineering,
and ramp-up services for photovoltaic cells and modules as well as
battery manufacturing plants. RCT Solutions has no Australian
operations.
The target, Wärtsilä Energy, is headquartered in Helsinki, Finland. It is
the energy storage business of the Finnish technology group
Wärtsilä and acts as a system integrator, combining battery cells
from leading manufacturers with its own energy management
software, power conversion technology, controls, and lifecycle
services to deliver complete, utility-scale battery energy storage
solutions for modern power systems. Wärtsilä Energy supplies
equipment and services in Australia through its wholly owned
subsidiary, Wärtsilä Energy Storage Australia Pty Ltd.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. There is no horizontal or vertical overlap between RCT
Solutions and Wärtsilä Energy in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
